 Hunter Henry (foot) will play in Week 10 against the Lions.
 Despite his listing with a limited practice on all three days this week, Henry was cleared from the injury report and is set for a normal role versus Detroit in Munich, Germany. Though he typically jostles each week for snaps and target share with promising rookie Eli Raridon, Henry remains one of New England’s most logical aerial threats in the red zone. Fantasy managers desperate for tight end help could do worse than throwing a dart with Henry.
 -  Tim Heaney

 A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) is listed as questionable for Week 10 against the Lions. 
 Despite his uncertain status, Brown, who was limited in all three practices during the week, made the trip across the Atlantic Ocean with the Pats before their game in Munich, Germany. The veteran has missed two straight contests, and New England may decide to rest him once again before the team’s Week 11 bye. Should Brown suit up, he would sit in the WR2/WR3 tiers against a Detroit secondary that’s improved lately but has been generally friendly to receivers most of the season. If Brown can’t go, DeMario Douglas would take that baton as the top target; Mack Hollins, Efton Chism, and Kyle Williams would see a boost into stronger Flex territory, and tight end Hunter Henry would slot into a more stream-worthy status.

 Hunter Henry (foot) was limited in Thursday’s practice. 
 He played off a questionable tag last week with a more checked practice report, so we’d be surprised if Henry didn’t go on Sunday. He has a real chance of being cleared off the injury report altogether on Friday after a pair of limited sessions to open the week.

 Hunter Henry (foot) was limited in Wednesday’s practice. 
 Henry played through the foot issue last week despite a severely limited practice regimen throughout the week. He only caught three passes for 35 yards, though the Pats failed to get much going on offense while the game was competitive. He should rebound as a high-end TE2 for his Week 10 date with the Lions.

 Hunter Henry caught 3-of-3 targets for 35 yards in the Patriots’ Week 9 loss to the Packers. 
 Henry was playing through a foot injury in this one, but still ended up leading all Patriots tight ends in routes run (22). Prior to his injury-shortened outing in Week 8, Henry was riding a four-game streak of double-digit PPR performances, but he wasn’t able to get there this week. Hopefully, he didn’t suffer any setbacks this week and will be a viable streaming option in what could be a plus matchup next week against the Lions.

In addition to Brown being out, the Patriots also declared RB TreVeyon Henderson, CB Charles Woods, OT Dametrious Crownover, and QB Behren Morton inactive for Week 9.

He didn’t practice Wednesday or Thursday, however, so it seems unlikely. Eli Raridon is inline to be the top tight end option if Henry can’t play.

 It’s looking like rookie Eli Raridon will operate as the Patriots’ No. 1 tight end in Week 9 against the Packers. Henry has not participated in football activities since injuring his foot early in Week 8 against the Dolphins. Raridon would warrant streaming TE1 consideration if he gets the start.

 Hunter Henry (foot) was not seen at the start of Wednesday’s practice. 
 Henry could ultimately get in a limited session later in the day, but this certainly looks like a DNP. The veteran tight end injured his foot early in the Pats’ Week 8 win over the Dolphins and did not return. Rookie Eli Raridon will take his spot in the lineup if Henry is unable to play this week. Raridon is averaging an impressive 13.3 yards per catch while mixing in behind Henry this year. He would immediately be in the TE2 mix if Henry is ruled out.

 Hunter Henry did not return to the Patriots’ Week 8 win over the Dolphins after suffering a foot injury in the second quarter. 
 This is particularly unfortunate because Henry was playing well early on, catching 3-of-3 targets for 30 yards. Drake Maye told reporters after the game that he is “worried” about his No. 1 tight end, but added that Henry was “walking around fine” with “a smile on his face” in the locker room post-game. Eli Raridon will be a streaming TE1 against the Packers next week if Henry cannot play.

 A.J. Brown (hamstring) is questionable to return in Week 10 against the Lions.
 Brown tried to gut it out through this issue early in the fourth quarter, but he ultimately walked off the field and into the locker room, likely ending his day. Even though he’s listed as questionable, we don’t expect him to return in a blowout loss. He will have a Week 11 bye to get healthy, though it’s looking like a lost season for the former superstar. Brown missed a month with a high-ankle injury early in the year, and now his lingering knee issue won’t go away, even as he tries to play through it. 
 -  Kyle Dvorchak

 Walker was ruled out on Saturday, paving the way for rookie Emmett Johnson to potentially see a bell cow role in a plus matchup against the Falcons. Walker should be considered no better than week to week after getting injured in Friday’s practice, but the team has expressed hope that this is nothing more than a one-week injury.  Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) is officially active against the Bills in Week 10. 
 That means all of Cooper Jr., Garrett Wilson, and Adonai Mitchell will be active.
